summary: Intermittent 429s for enterprise customer after edge TLS rewrite / proxy header normalization
summary_details: Customer DataWave reports sudden increase in 429 throttles starting 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC. The errors are intermittent but concentrated on a subset of API keys and appear correlated with requests routed through the customer's new proxy stack that rewrites TLS/SNI and normalizes headers.
description:
Issue summary:
DataWave (enterprise) began seeing intermittent 429s for production inference calls. Patterns point to edge proxy normalization (TLS SNI rewrite + Host header rewrite) that causes our rate-limiter fingerprint to collapse distinct connections into a single accounting bucket for certain request paths.

Impact:
- Several production services at DataWave experienced elevated 429 rates across both streaming and batch routes, resulting in degraded throughput and increased client retries.
- Affected a subset of API keys for the org (3 keys), ~6% of traffic; customer reports visible user-facing timeouts.

Environment:
- Customer on enterprise plan using Dedicated ingress via customer-managed edge.
- Traffic path: client -> customer edge (TLS terminate & rewrite) -> customer NAT -> Redwood edge LB -> origin.
- Region: us-east-1, prod.

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) Use an API key associated with DataWave org and send concurrent streaming starts (~150 concurrent short sessions) from clients behind the customer's new proxy that performs TLS SNI rewrite and forces Host header to canonical host.
2) Observe a spike of 429 responses from our edge after ~30s of sustained concurrency.
3) Re-run with identical concurrency but bypassing the customer's proxy (direct internet) — 429s disappear.

Observed logs / headers (sample):
- 429 response body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded", "message":"Quota exhausted for tenant"}
- Response headers: X-RateLimit-Limit: 6000, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 2026-03-12T23:15:00Z
- Edge log snippet (abridged): "edge_id=us-e-09 src_ip=10.3.18.22 sni=analytics-cust.internal rewrite_host=api.redwood.example key_id=ak_3U7... fingerprint=fingerprint-237"

Notes on anomaly:
- Fingerprint collisions: Our rate-limiter attaches a fingerprint per connection that includes source IP + TLS SNI + Host header in order to isolate refill windows. The customer's proxy rewrites SNI to a shared SNI and sets a canonical Host header which makes multiple distinct client identities evaluate to the same fingerprint.
- In combination with NAT and ephemeral keys, the aggregated token accounting causes a subset of the customer's keys to report Remaining=0 even though per-key usage should be separate.

Investigation notes (SRE):
- Replayed traffic through a mirror of customer proxy in staging and reproduced elevated 429s once header/SNI rewrite occurred.
- Correlated with edge access logs: multiple api_key values map to a single rate-limiter bucket id when rewrite_host and sni_override fields are present.
- Confirmed the rate-limiter logic relies on SNI+Host for additional entropy to separate client windows as a defense against pooled-NAT aggregation.
- Hypothesis: the recent optional proxy-normalize feature triggers for certain ALB configurations, enabling header rewrite. This interacts poorly for customers doing TLS rewrite on their side.

Customer quotes (from support call):
- "After we flipped the new proxy into production, our jobs started failing with 429s — halting nightly scoring pipelines. Bypassing the proxy fixes it." — DataWave infra lead

Engineering notes: 
- Related code path: rate-limiter fingerprinting lives in service edge code (controller/rate/fingerprint.go). See PR that added proxy-normalize toggle: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1824.
- Quick mitigation: allowlist the customer's ingress by disabling SNI+Host coalescing for that tenant so per-key buckets are maintained. Longer-term fix: change fingerprint to prefer api_key_id + connection-id when api_key is present, falling back to sni+host for anonymous traffic.

Actions taken so far:
- 2026-03-12 12:40 UTC: Support contacted DataWave and confirmed reproduction.
- 2026-03-13 03:10 UTC: SRE mirrored proxy behavior in staging and reproduced 429s.
- 2026-03-13 09:00 UTC: Applied a temporary tenant-level exception on rate-limiter to stop SNI-based coalescing for DataWave keys. 429s dropped to baseline.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is the tenant-level exception safe across scale? We need to audit whether disabling SNI coalescing will increase memory/slot usage for the rate-limiter for large orgs.
- Should we make proxy-normalize opt-in for customers that perform TLS rewrite?

Customer impact status:
- Currently mitigated (temporary exception applied). Customer has resumed nightly jobs but requests a permanent fix and guidance on recommended proxy configuration.

Suggested resolution plan:
1) Short-term: Keep tenant exception in place and monitor token/fingerprint table growth for DataWave (SRE).
2) Mid-term: Implement fingerprint logic change to prefer api_key_id when available (Engineering, priority change PR).
3) Docs/Support: Add a support note in KB to recommend avoiding TLS SNI rewrite or to use our documented proxy flags (edge-proxy: preserve-sni=false with per-tenant exceptions) and provide a config checklist.

Resolution notes:
- Temporary tenant exception applied (2026-03-13) reduced 429s to baseline; monitoring continues.
- Engineering tasked to produce PR for api_key_id-first fingerprint by 2026-03-20.

References and cross-references:
- Slack: #support - thread SUP-776543 (https://slack.redwood/inbox/support/threads/CH12345-776543)
- GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1824
- Confluence runbook: confluence.redwood.internal/Runbooks/RateLimiterFingerprinting
comments: 2026-03-12 Maya Patel: Initial report received from DataWave. They provided a sample session trace and said bypassing their proxy removes the issue.
2026-03-12 Samir Desai: Acknowledged, creating staging mirror to reproduce. Marking as P1 due to enterprise impact.
2026-03-13 SRE on-call (J. Huang): Reproduced in staging when proxy rewrites SNI -> confirms fingerprint collapse. Temporary tenant exception deployed, awaiting customer validation.
2026-03-13 DataWave (infra lead): Confirmed jobs resumed after exception. Asked for permanent fix timeline and config checklist.
2026-03-14 Eng (A. Lopez): Spun up a small design doc to change fingerprint to api_key-first. Targeting PR by 2026-03-20.
final_resolution: Temporary tenant-level exception applied to disable SNI+Host coalescing for DataWave keys; engineering to implement api_key_first fingerprinting as permanent fix. KB entry and proxy configuration guidance to be published after PR merges.
